Relics & Rites

Every item, potion, elixir, throwable, scroll, manual and reagent, all 213 spells, and every area a spell can cover, drawn from data alone and put on the new hex floors. The page compares five ways to draw objects and five ways to draw casts. Code in this folder made every picture on this page. Nothing in frontend/ or character-proposals/ was changed. This folder only imports from them.

The Drowned Vault at 195 px wide, ×2, with Call Lightning.
§

The short version

what to look at, what I'd pick

Today the game draws items with gen/textures/itemIcon.ts, which is 15 silhouettes with a material and a rarity frame. It draws spells with render/vfx/spells.ts, which is spheres, boxes and rings. There are 99 consumable stacks and they produce 12 distinct icons. Cone, chain, vortex and sigil spells fall back to the melee arc. Loot never appears on the map. Every approach below reads one recipe table and the game's own data: damage hues, surface palettes, rarity and the 76 actions, copied by a tool rather than by hand. From that it produces a distinct picture for every one of the 651 objects and every spell. None of them needs save data.

ObjectsO1 · Pixel icon grammar

It is the same engine as the recommended character approach (A), so loot and heroes look like one game. It covers all 651 objects in 105 ms, about 0.16 ms each. One recipe gives the inventory icon at ×2 and the loot on the floor at 18 px. Every element carries a 5×5 mark as well as its hue.

CastsS1 particles + S2 hex decals

S2 draws the ground: exactly which hexes a spell covers, which serves the dice-are-real pillar. S1 draws the air: the projectile, the beam and the burst. Adding both to an M3 frame costs 9–16 ms on top of a 2 ms base. In M1, S1 is 0.2 ms per frame and S2 is 2.4 ms.

When it must stand upS4 · Toon meshes

Walls of fire, Moonbeam's column and a cone of prisms are volumes. In M1, S4 draws them at 0.3 ms per frame, with a median of 16 draw calls in the arena and a worst case of 77. It is the upgrade path for render/vfx/spells.ts and uses the same kinds of primitives.

One recipe, five renderers

lib/items.js → lib/parts.js → objects/*

This is the idea from character-proposals, extended: a thing's look is data. Each object has a short recipe, which lib/parts.js compiles once into vector geometry: lathes (bottles, helm domes), polygons (blades, book covers), bars (hafts, rolled scroll ends), ellipses (gems, seals) and ink strokes (sigils). Each of the five object approaches is only a way of drawing that geometry, so they cannot drift apart. A new potion is one row.

// lib/items.js — potions from data/consumables/potions.ts: the family picks the vessel, the effect picks the liquid
potionGreaterHealing: { flask: 'round', liquid: '#c8323c', fill: 0.85, cork: 'wax', tier: 2 }
alchemistFire:        { flask: 'grenade', liquid: dmg('fire'), fill: 0.8, cork: 'rag' }      // the game's fire hue, never retyped
reagentBeholderIris:  { form: 'eye', c: '#6a3a6a', iris: '#d0a030' }                   // one of 27 form grammars
// lib/spells.js — one row per spell: school · element · delivery · shape · size · surface · list · source
Fireball          |evo|fire     |projectile|sphere  |20 |fire |arcane |game   // 'game' rows take the sim's own radius: 3.2
Cone of Cold      |evo|cold     |self      |cone    |60 |     |arcane |srd
Bursting Sinew    |nec|necrotic |target    |sphere  |5  |     |arcane |bg3    // BG3-only: drafted, marked, CHECK
game data (snapshot tool)→recipe row→parts: lathe · poly · bar · ell · strokes · mark→O1 … O5→+ rarity rim / halo

Measured, not assumed tools/snapshot-game.mjs · tools/audit.mjs

The game's data is copied by tools/snapshot-game.mjs, which imports frontend/src/data under Node and writes lib/game.js. Nothing is retyped by hand. tools/audit.mjs then fails if any id in the game, or any row in docs/references, has no look. It passes at 100%.

What the game draws today

tools/baseline.mjs runs gen/textures/itemIcon.ts itself

These are not screenshots and not a reconstruction. tools/baseline.mjs imports the game's own generateItemIcon and generateStackIcon under Node and writes their pixels. The first sheet is all 54 bases. The second is all 99 stacks, which produce 12 distinct images. A Potion of Speed and Fury in a Bottle are the same icon. So are Scroll of Fireball and Scroll of Bless, and a Unicorn Horn and a pouch of Mugwort.

Rows, in order: potions and throwables share the flask, all 36 scrolls share the scroll, and reagents and solvents share the pouch. Rarity is the only difference. The Legendary frame is gold, which is correct.

O1

Pixel icon grammar

objects/O1-pixel · recommended

This is character-proposals' pixel engine (lib/pixel.js) fed the shared parts. Each part becomes a mask, painted with a hue-shifted ramp shaded from its own silhouette. The whole icon then gets a selective outline. Glass is a rim and a highlight, so the liquid shows through it, with a meniscus line on top. Every element carries a 5×5 mark (lib/marks.js), the pixel twin of each damage type's glyph. It appears on an elixir's tag, a scroll's seal and a spell icon's corner, because visual-language Q3 says hue alone is never enough. Rarity recolours the outline, and Very Rare and above adds a halo, the same rule the characters follow.

parts→masks at any size→ramp + silhouette shading→glass rim · meniscus · marks→sel-out→rarity rim / halo

One of each kind ×3, then ×1 as on a phone

All 54 item bases

Potions and throwables the vessel carries the family, the liquid carries the effect

Healing climbs through the tiers from round flask to Erlenmeyer to decanter, and Supreme glows. Cures are slim vials with a label. Mana is tall. Emergency draughts are squat and caged in iron. Buffs are gourds. Throwables have a rag fuse, a metal case or a ceramic shell. Potion of Speed and Draught of Valour were first drawn yellow, which looked gold on the page, so they were moved to quicksilver and ivory.

Elixirs and crafted potions references/potions.md — no item in code yet

An elixir lasts until a long rest, so it gets a vessel no potion uses: a tall decanter with a tag. The first render had only colour to tell the resistances apart, which breaks the rule, so each tag now carries its type's mark. No rarity was invented for these, so they show as Common.

Scrolls and manuals the 36 in the game, and the 32 martial actions as manuals

The paper and the wax give the spell list: arcane is blue wax, divine crimson, primal green. The sigil in the middle is generated from the spell's id (lib/sigil.js). Its frame comes from the school, eight learnable shapes, and its strokes from a hash, so every spell is unique. The seal carries the element's mark. Radiant ink was invisible on parchment in the first render, so pale inks are now darkened while keeping their hue. A manual is a book in its class's leather, stamped with the action's VFX family.

The whole catalogue as scrolls 213, by list, ×1

Reagents and solvents 27 form grammars

Spell icons 212, grouped by area shape

Each icon is a medallion. It shows the school frame, the sigil in the element's hue, the element mark bottom-left, and the area pictogram bottom-right (sphere, cone, line, cube, aura or wall). At 32 px the sigil is busy. It reads better at 40 px or more, or in O2.

Rarity

0.16 msper object (651 in 105 ms)
32×32icon, any size
18 pxas floor loot
23element marks

For

  • The same pixel language as the A characters, so hero and loot are drawn the same way.
  • Legible at 18–32 px. The vessel, form and mark all carry meaning without colour.
  • Cheapest of the five: the whole catalogue costs a tenth of a second, then it is cached.
  • One output serves the inventory, the loot on the floor and the shop.

Against

  • Spell sigils crowd at 32 px.
  • Text glyphs are impossible, so the 5×5 marks are an approximation of the game's glyphs.
  • Shapes are code. A new kind of thing, such as a new reagent form, is a small grammar, not a row.
O2

Manuscript vector

objects/O2-vector · SVG

The same parts drawn as SVG: flat fills bordered in ink, with engraved hatching on the side away from the light, and glyphs set as real type. This is the game's existing UI language, ink on vellum like the sprite in ui/icons.ts. It is crisp at any size, and it is the only approach that can print the game's own glyphs (✦ ❆ ⚡ ☠ ☾ ☀).

0.06 msmarkup per object
∞sizes
real glyphson tags and marks

For

  • It matches the UI it would sit in (Hoard rows, the shop, tooltips).
  • It scales to the character sheet's large slots without a new render.
  • It shows the game's real damage glyphs.

Against

  • Next to pixel-art characters on the map it looks like a sticker, not a thing lying on the floor.
  • Hatching needs about 40 px to read, and turns to noise at 18 px.
  • Pairing O2 in the UI with O1 on the map would give two looks for one item.
O3

Voxel mini-models

objects/O3-voxel · objects/voxelize.js

The parts are voxelised on a 28³ grid. A lathe becomes a solid of revolution, and a polygon becomes an extrusion as thick as its part. Only faces that touch air are meshed. Each model is lit and rendered from a fixed 3/4 camera through one shared WebGL context. Glass is a see-through shell. Rarity is a coloured ring under the object, because a voxel outline cannot carry it.

1.9 msper object
28³grid
1WebGL context for all

For

  • A real volume, reusable by O4 and by the M2 voxel map.
  • Potions read as solid glass bottles.

Against

  • At 32 px, sigils and marks lose their strokes to the voxel grid.
  • Thin things (rings, bowstrings, feathers) break up.
  • Twelve times the cost of O1 for a less legible picture.
O4

Sprite-stacked loot

objects/O4-stack · O3's volume, sliced

O3's volume is cut into horizontal slices. Each slice is rotated in 2D and drawn one pixel above the last. The result is pixel output at any angle, with no WebGL. Its one real use is Legendary loot that slowly turns on the floor. Motion Q2 forbids motion on anything that happens often, so every ordinary drop must stay still.

3.1 msper object, per angle
∞angles

For

  • Any angle, fully pixel, cheap once sliced.

Against

  • The muddiest of the five: flat items such as swords and scrolls read poorly from their side.
  • The slowest per object.
O5

Lathe & extrude toon 3D

objects/O5-lathe3d · baked, cached by recipe hash

Bottles are real LatheGeometry. Blades, plates and covers are extruded outlines, and bars are capsules. Everything gets character-proposals' toon ramp and inverted-hull outline, and renders at 32 px. Each bake is cached under a hash of the recipe, so it is paid once per distinct object. That is E's idea, applied to items.

0.71 msper object, uncached
≈0 mscache hit

For

  • The best bottles of the five, because they are true solids of revolution.
  • The same meshes could stand in an M1 scene as real objects.

Against

  • Softer than O1. The toon outline is thin at 32 px.
  • Decals such as sigils and marks are planes laid in front of the model, not part of it.
✦

Casts, as data over time

casts/cast.js · one timeline, five renderers

A cast is a spell's look, plus a caster and a target, and from those lib/hexarea.js works out the cells it covers. casts/cast.js turns that into emitters on a 0–1 timeline:

  1. Telegraph: a rule on the covered cells, never a fill.
  2. Release: the projectile, beam, bolt or sweep.
  3. Impact: the burst, or each cell as the sweep reaches it.
  4. Aftermath: a zone, a column, or the surface the game says it leaves behind.

particlesAt(cast, t) is a pure function of time, so any frame can be drawn on its own, identically on every device. Every approach below renders the same 18 casts at the same four moments, in the same arena. Each approach's matrix is a tall sheet, so scroll inside it.

look + caster + target→hexarea cells→emitters: telegraph · travel · beam · burst · sweep · column · ring · wall · zone · surface→S1 … S5

The 18 casts are: Fire Bolt · Ray of Frost · Chain Lightning · Fireball · Cone of Cold (hex 60° and 5e 53°) · Lightning Bolt (1 wide) · Sunbeam (2 wide) · Thunderwave (cube) · Moonbeam (cylinder zone) · Spirit Guardians (aura) · Wall of Fire · Cloudkill · Grease · Mass Healing Word · Hex · Shocking Grasp · Spiritual Weapon.
Motion Q2 allows only the brief cast to move. Zones and surfaces are state: fire and acid get at most a slow shimmer.

S1

Pixel particles

casts/S1-pixel-particles · the air half

The particles are drawn as single pixels and tiny pixel shapes, with a different shape for each element: an ember, a shard, a spark cross, a drip, a puff, a mote, a wisp. They are drawn additively, after lighting, and depth-tested against walls. The projectile head, and a burst's core, add real light to the room through the renderer's light pass. S1 paints nothing on the floor except the surface a cast leaves behind.

1.3 msmedian added per frame (p95 10.7)
0.2 msin M1 as pixel points

For

  • It reads as pixel art and lights the room around it.
  • The cheapest cast approach in both renderers.

Against

  • It cannot tell you which hex is hit. A dust telegraph is vague.
  • Walls and columns are only rising embers.
S2

Hex footprint decals

casts/S2-hex-decals · the ground half · recommended with S1

The area is drawn as hex cells on the floor. The telegraph is a rule along the outside edge plus a sparse dither. At impact, each cell washes in the element's hue at the moment the effect reaches it, so a cone visibly travels outward. Afterwards the zone or surface stays as floor state. This is literally "how a spell looks on the hex tile system", and it is the one approach that can always state exactly which cells were hit, which is what the dice-are-real pillar asks for.

S2 in M1 the same ground functions, baked to a floor decal per frame

5.2 msmedian added per frame in M3 (p95 20.9)
2.4 msin M1, including the texture bake

For

  • It shows the rules exactly, which suits a game about visible dice.
  • Surfaces follow the ruling: a low-saturation tint plus a distinct texture (casts/surfaces.js).

Against

  • It draws nothing in the air. On its own a Fire Bolt is invisible until it lands.
  • The per-frame bake in M1 would want caching per cell-set in the game.
S3

Continuous field

casts/S3-field · soft SDF + noise

A soft signed-distance field is built from the same cells, plus noise. A Fireball becomes a round, ragged scorch rather than a set of hexes. The telegraph is a single smooth contour. Travelling parts are radial glows. It is the prettiest ground, and it misleads: the soft edge covers cells the rules do not.

17.0 msmedian added per frame
189 msp95, the worst of all

For

  • Organic shapes, the most "magical" floor.

Against

  • It shows an area the dice did not roll against.
  • Every covered pixel sums every cell, so a large cloud's frame cost spikes. That is measured above.
S4

Toon meshes

casts/S4-toon-mesh · M1 only

Every emitter becomes a primitive with a toon ramp and an emissive colour: a sphere head with a trailing cone, cylinders for beams and columns, a torus for an aura, hex prisms that rise under a sweep, boxes for a wall. The telegraph is the hex rim as 3D lines. This is the same primitive family as today's render/vfx/spells.ts, extended to every shape and driven by the same cells.

0.3 msbuild + render
16 / 77draw calls, median / max
≤2,440triangles

For

  • The only approach that stands a wall, a column or a cone up as a volume.
  • A direct upgrade path for the code that exists.

Against

  • It reads as 3D shapes, not pixel art, next to A's sprites.
  • Draw calls grow with cells: 77 for the worst cast.

These are S1's particles as instanced lit cubes: one draw call for every particle of every cast.

Areas on hexes

lib/hexarea.js · drawn from the cell lists

The sim has one area shape today: a Euclidean disc (aoeRadius and SurfaceGrid.paint) over square tiles. lib/hexarea.js gives the hex versions of it and of every shape the catalogue uses. The functions are pure and import nothing from window, so the sim could own them under R1. The diagrams below are drawn from the functions' output, and the counts are measured.

ShapeMeasuredWhat it means
Disc r 3.2 (Fireball)37 squares → 37 hexesAt the game's Fireball radius, the move to hexes keeps the same number of cells.
Disc r 1.8 (Cleave) · r 3 (Stinking Cloud)9 → 13 · 29 → 37Smaller discs grow on hexes (+44% and +28%). A balance question for the hex pass, not answered here.
Cone 60° hex vs 53° 5e6/6 · 10/9 · 22/18 at 15/20/30 ftThe same at 15 ft. The 60° wedge follows grid lines and takes 1–4 more cells at the rim.
Line, 2 wideone-sided bandOn hexes the next row is 0.866 away, so a symmetric band is 1 or 3 cells wide. A 2-wide line leans to one side. Found by the first test, which returned 3.
Cuben × n axial lozengeA square cannot be drawn on hexes, so this is the closest grid-true shape.

On the new floors

map/scenes.js · M3 and M1, all eight biomes

These are real hex dungeons from character-proposals' generator. Each scene has the A-sprite party, foes, loot on the floor (O1 icons at 18 px, each with a rarity ring beneath), an opened chest, a surface pair (grease meeting fire, and a web), and one signature cast per biome drawn as S1 + S2. All shots are at t = 0.6, the moment of impact. M3 is a copy of character-proposals' render2d.js (map/render2d-fx.js) with three hooks added: a ground overlay, a post-light draw, and extra lights. The original is untouched.

M3 · pure 2D 330×220, ×2

One Fireball, four moments t = 0.12 · 0.42 · 0.6 · 0.92

M1 · three.js 660×460 at ½ resolution

Loot at map scale ×1 as on a phone, and ×3

Loot lies as the O1 icon at 18 px, fanned inside one hex. A ring beneath each item shows its rarity, the same rule as the icon's rim, and only Legendary is gold. At ×1 the individual items are hard to name, but the ring says "loot, and how good". Today drops never touch the map (sim/Run.ts:collect), so showing them is a design decision for you. See the plan.

The plan

full version in README.md · not started; each step needs your go-ahead

Recommendation: O1 for every object, and S1 + S2 for casts. Keep S4 in reserve for the volume spells (walls, columns) if the game stays on M1.

  1. Recipes into data.
    • Add vis to StackDef and to the potion, throwable, reagent and solvent rows.
    • Add a look (school, element, delivery, area) to ActionDef beside vfx.
    The drafts are in lib/items.js and lib/spells.js. R3 holds, and there is no save change.
  2. Port O1 to gen/textures/itemIcon.ts, replacing the silhouettes. lib/parts.js and lib/marks.js become gen/ modules. R1 holds: a canvas factory, and no ui/ imports.
  3. Port S2's ground functions into render/vfx/areaEffects.ts and S1's particles into render/vfx/spells.ts. This fills the cone, chain, vortex and sigil families that fall back to melee today.
  4. Cone, line, cube and wall as sim shapes belong to the hex pass and pass B. lib/hexarea.js is ready for them, but they are not scoped here.

Open questions for you

  • Should loot appear on the map at all? Today drops go straight to the inventory. The pictures show it working, but that is a design change.
  • Cones on hexes: 60° or 53°? The 60° wedge follows the grid. The 5e cone is 1–4 cells smaller at 20–30 ft.
  • Small discs grow on hexes (Cleave 9 → 13 cells). Should radii be retuned in the hex pass?
  • The eight BG3-only spells are drafted. Confirm their areas and elements.
  • Elixirs have no rarity in code or the references. They show as Common until you set one.

Considered and rejected

  • Icon packs (game-icons.net and similar). They are CC-BY, which breaks the sourcing rule in asset-pipeline.md, and they are the "image per item" approach you want to avoid.
  • AI image generation per item or spell. It is not deterministic, does not run offline, and has the same provenance problem.
  • Colour-only variants of one flask, which is effectively today's approach. It fails visual-language Q3, and the baseline shows the result: 12 images for 99 stacks.
  • Animated idle loot (bobbing, sparkling). Motion Q2 forbids it for anything common. Only Legendary may turn (O4).
